title: Turn an angle grinder's guard to face the operator and clamp it
instruction: Make the angle grinder safe for the operator standing at the marked spot.
context: Angle grinders are used every day by welders, fabricators and construction laborers, and a disc can shatter at high speed. The guard is the barrier between the disc and the operator: OSHA's abrasive wheel standard (29 CFR 1910.215) says Type 27 and 28 wheels shall be used only with a safety guard located between wheel and operator during use, and SafeWork SA says the guard should cover half of the disc, be positioned between the disc and the operator and be secure. A guard left facing the wrong way, or unclamped so it can turn in use, exposes the operator to fragments and sparks.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases: x forward, y to the robot's left; heights above the table top. A 115 mm angle grinder (generic brand, 1.55 kg including its disc: teal plastic motor housing 5.8 cm across and 18 cm long, black rear cap 5.4 cm across, grey cast gear head 6.2 x 7.2 x 5.8 cm, black side handle 2.3 x 11.5 cm, 43 mm steel collar; 27.7 cm long) lies on its side on the table with the motor along -y and its spindle vertical through (25.5, 12.0); friction about 0.6. A 115 x 6 mm printed grinding disc (0.12 kg, part of the 1.55 kg) sits 7.4 cm above the table on the spindle under a 1 cm clamp nut. A zinc-plated steel guard hood (0.18 kg; 3 mm plate, 6.2 cm inner radius, 3.2 cm tall 2.5 mm skirt over 190 degrees of the disc) sits on the collar and turns about the spindle; its closed side starts facing +x (away from the operator). A yellow adjusting tab (2.5 x 0.8 x 2.4 cm) stands 2 cm above the skirt's rim 60 degrees anticlockwise (seen from above) of the closed side, and a red flat clamp lever (5.5 x 1.4 x 0.8 cm, 20 g, over-centre) is hinged on the skirt 9 cm up, 30 degrees anticlockwise of the closed side, shut (flat). Flat, the lever clamps the guard; raised past 45 degrees it snaps open and frees it. A flat printed OPERATOR mat (14 x 10 cm) lies at (11.5, 12.0), 14 cm from the spindle towards -x (towards the robot). A second layout (B, mirrored: spindle at (25.5, -10.0), motor along +y, mat at (25.5, -24.0), guard starting at bearing 150 degrees) is selected with TASK_VARIANT=B.
scoring: Judged from a photo and a protractor; the score is the state at the current step (no best score). 1.0 (success, held 2 s): the lever is flat (within 8 degrees) and the guard's closed-side bisector faces the operator mat within 30 degrees, the grinder is within 2 cm and 10 degrees of where it started and not tipped (tilt under 10 degrees), both tool points are at least 13 cm from the spindle axis (or above 25 cm over the table), and nothing below was violated. 0.75: lever flat, guard within 45 degrees. 0.5: guard within 90 degrees of the operator (lever any). 0.25: the lever is raised 60 degrees or more. 0 otherwise. Any of these (latched) caps the score at 0.25: a fingertip within 6 mm of the disc; the guard is turned more than 10 degrees while the lever is flat; the grinder is shoved more than 4 cm, turned more than 20 degrees or tilted more than 30 degrees.
reset_notes: Clamp lever flat (shut), guard with its closed side towards +x (layout A), grinder on the table with its motor along -y and the disc up, OPERATOR mat in front of it (towards the robot). Nothing is consumed.
fidelity: Rigid bodies, 240 Hz physics, 20 Hz control. The grinder is one articulation: the guard turns on a revolute joint about the spindle, the lever on a hinge. Task code does the clamp (the guard is held while the lever is flat), the lever's over-centre snap (45 degrees open, 40 shut) and the bearing and violation checks. The disc is inert; nothing is ground. Real parts: 115 mm grinder 1.55 kg, 115 x 6 mm disc; same size and mass here.
scores: Dream-1 run: refused by the Dream service at the first request (DA-4000, unsafe instruction in this scene), no action taken, nothing scored; scripted demo: 1.0 in 1,159 steps (layout A); ablations: no motion 0, guard turn with the lever shut 0, guard turned two thirds of the way 0.50, guard turned the wrong way 0.25
